To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we can find a very small subset of filters in one-branch networks that are responsible for the removal of a specific degradation, and that these filters are important for determining the specific network function; 2) the task of degradation prediction is realized by these discriminable filters without explicit supervised training; 3) these findings can help better understand the network behaviors in blind SR, and also help design more efficient networks and diagnose networks for blind SR.
We propose a new integral gradient method, Filter Attribution based on Integral Gradient, for finding the most discriminant filters in blind super-resolution networks.
we propose a new integral gradient method for finding discriminative filters for specific degradations in blind super-resolution networks.
